meta.title: Dossier 0.7.0
meta.lede: Dossier rebuilt as one Go binary, with six designed kinds, verdicts, search, diagrams, a studio, and a new showcase. Every gate passed, and the call is ship.

parts.markdown: 0.7 replaces the Node generator with a single CGO-free Go binary built around five concepts: kind, section, item, facet, and decisions. It installs through Homebrew, npm, or an archive, and every 0.6 document still builds.

parts.title: Highlights
rows: Six designed kinds (brainstorm, plan, review, release, incident, and brief) each carry their own fields, facets, sections, and way to decide. Teams add their own with `--kinds DIR`.
Picks, verdicts, and a document choice all write one reply line, which `dossier decisions apply` reads back into the model.
Search, verdicts from the keyboard, one brand color, timelines, charts, and diagrams laid out as SVG at build time, with no external requests.
`dossier serve` edits the page in place as drafts, keeps decisions in SQLite in step across tabs, and edits the model as JSON in CodeMirror.
One command catalog projects to the CLI, an MCP server, and a generated skill, all answering one result envelope.
They validate and build with a warning per old block, and `dossier upgrade` maps them onto the new kinds.

items.title: Go checks
items.summary: Formatting, vet, staticcheck, errcheck, the race-enabled tests, and a CGO-free build all passed.

facets.label: How checked
facets.markdown: `make check` in `core`, which also drift-checks generated code and the vendored Graphviz.

facets.label: Result
facets.markdown: Every package passed, with the reader at 19.2 KB of its 20 KB budget and the stylesheet at 29.1 KB of 30.

items.title: Showcase fixtures
items.summary: All seven example documents build with no warnings and match their HTML and Markdown goldens.

facets.label: How checked
facets.markdown: `TestExamples` and `TestExampleReplies` build the showcase the way a reader gets it and paste a reply into each decision document.

facets.label: Result
facets.markdown: Seven documents, six kinds, no warnings, and the largest page under 100 KB of its 120 KB budget.

items.title: 0.6 imports
items.summary: All 17 legacy fixtures upgrade to models that pass the strict 0.7 checks.

facets.label: How checked
facets.markdown: `TestLegacyFixtures` upgrades each 0.6 document and compares it with its golden.

facets.label: Result
facets.markdown: 17 of 17 upgrade strictly onto their kinds' vocabularies.

items.title: React package tests
items.summary: The wrapper renders through the binary and reads reader messages, verdicts included.

facets.label: How checked
facets.markdown: `npm test` in `packages/react`, including the reply cases shared with the Go parser.

items.title: Distribution dry run
items.summary: Six archives, their checksums, the Homebrew formula, and seven npm packages build and install.

facets.label: How checked
facets.markdown: `make dist-check` cross-compiles every target, runs the formula's test commands on an archive, and installs the npm packages from tarballs.

facets.label: Result
facets.markdown: Every check printed ok, and each archive carries `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

items.title: Reader and studio in a browser
items.summary: Every page in light, dark, and at phone width, and every studio tool, worked by hand.

facets.label: How checked
facets.markdown: The manual QA guide: search, picks, keyboard verdicts, the ship warning, two-tab sync, reply import, facets, conflicts, the accent, and the Model JSON editor.

facets.label: Result
facets.markdown: All passed. A framed page reported its verdicts, and the React package accepted the message.

parts.markdown: 0.7.0 replaces the 0.6 npm package's JavaScript API with the binary. A project that needs 0.6 pins it, and 0.6 documents build on either version.
